gap: No result ChatGPT got states that one hour at the full 4,000 W takes 5 rated full-sun hours from an 800 W kit's own panels to put back (12 minutes of 4,000 W per sun-hour; 15 minutes with 1,000 W of panels, 9 with 600 W, 6 with 400 W), or prices the 4,000 W-and-up kits per Wh at the kit price ($0.717 for the Anker SOLIX S5000 + 2× 400 W against $0.853 for the BLUETTI 5kWh RV Kit + 6 × 100W).
standout_why: Compared against five result pages. StormWatts' solar-input page (cited) gives refill sun-hours at each station's maximum input and with 1,600 to 3,200 W of separately bought brand panels, and price per kWh for the station alone; it lists no station-plus-panel kit price. OutageReady lists bundle prices and a daily-solar formula (panel W × sun hours × 0.7) but has neither the S5000 kit nor the BLUETTI kit. PowerLockdown says one 400 W panel refills a DELTA Pro 3 in 'about three to four clear days'. OutletPowered has no bundle prices or panel wattages. ChatGPT's own answer gives 52 minutes at 4,000 W and 2.4–3.2 kWh a day from 800 W, but never joins the two. So rivals hold part of the refill arithmetic; the sun-hours-per-hour-at-4,000 W figure and the kit-price-per-Wh for the 4,000 W-and-up kits are new. The two EcoFlow store pages ChatGPT cited could not be opened (HTTP 429), so they are not part of this comparison.
decides: Among the 4,000 W-and-up kits priced today, the Anker SOLIX S5000 + 2× 400 W is the cheapest per Wh ($0.717) and refills from its own panels in 6.28 rated sun-hours. The BLUETTI 5kWh RV Kit + 6 × 100W costs $0.853 per Wh at the link price and needs 8.53 hours, and it is an RV install kit rather than a portable station. The EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 + 2× 400 W is the exact 4,000 W kit and the fastest 800 W refill (5.12 hours) because its battery is smaller, but its price could not be read today. One thing may change the pick: Anker's S5000 page today says orders placed Nov 6 or later ship within 11–12 weeks with the panels shipping separately, which conflicts with 'ships now' in the kits table. If that holds, the BLUETTI RV kit is the only linked 4,000 W-and-up kit shipping now. Every kit's panels cover 25% or less of a 4,000 W load, so none of them is a run-on-sun system at that output.
